title: utilz doctor's checks each become a function of their own, and run_doctor only coordinates (Thin Coordinator, PFIC)
body:
## What

`run_doctor` (`opt/utilz/lib/common.sh:1329-1942` at 0109's close, `0946cd4f`) is one function that holds every doctor check inline: UTILZ_HOME, which tree this is, the directory structure, `bin/utilz`, the PATH configuration, the installed utilities, the external dependencies (with the platform notes, the crate probe and menuz's build tools), install integrity, and the summary. Each check's file and tool I/O, its decision rules and its output are all written in the coordinator.

## Why

hv's ruling, 26 Oct 2026, through molt-vc: it goes into 2.14.4, and now. "If we don't do it today, it'll get forgotten and then snowball. Fix it now, please." vc's critic leg on 0109 v2 flagged it (IN-AG-THIN-COORD-001, IN-AG-PFIC-001). It predates 0109.

## Design

The constraints, from hv's ruling through vc, bind:

- **Each check is a function of its own, and `run_doctor` only coordinates**: it prints the version line, runs the checks in today's order, totals their issues, and prints the summary and the exit.
- **A check never reports its count through its exit status.** Under `set -euo pipefail` a non-zero return from a bare call ends doctor, and a status stops at 255. A check adds to the coordinator's count instead (run_doctor's own `issues`, which bash's dynamic scope lets a callee update, or one named global), and it returns non-zero only when it could not run at all. Bash 3.2: no namerefs.
- **PFIC where it pays**: a decision that needs no I/O (which tree this is, whether a manifest is current, which dependencies are missing once their entries are read) sits in a function without I/O, and the reads sit at the check's edge. Do not split further than "each check its own function".
- **Behaviour-preserving**: doctor's report and exit status do not change, line for line, on every fixture the suite drives. The suite, unchanged, is the proof, along with a before-and-after diff of `bin/utilz doctor` on the dev tree, which may differ only in the version line's sha.
- **0110 lands on top**: its three silent exits are fixed in the extracted functions, with their own red and green.

cc's design, approved by utilz-vc (26 Oct), and corrected before any code to say exactly what the change does:

- **One function per section of today's report**, in common.sh's DOCTOR COMMAND section, after `_doctor_dep_note` and before `run_doctor`, under one header comment (DOCTOR'S CHECKS, issue 0111) that says what they share and why each returns 0. Each holds its section as it stands, from its `Checking ...` title through its reads, decisions and lines to its closing blank line: `_doctor_check_utilz_home`, `_doctor_check_tree`, `_doctor_check_dirs` (the directory structure), `_doctor_check_dispatcher` (`bin/utilz`), `_doctor_check_path` (PATH, with the link set's health, which prints under PATH's title and counts its own issue), `_doctor_check_utilities` (the installed utilities), `_doctor_check_dependencies` (the yq walk and its notes, exiftool, the crate probe, menuz's build tools and the verdict) and `_doctor_check_integrity` (install integrity with CI's recorded verdict, and the blank line before its title, which it prints today).
- **`run_doctor` coordinates**: the title, the rule and the version line; `have_yq`, resolved once as today; each check called bare, in today's order; then the summary and the exit status, as today.
- **The checks share `run_doctor`'s locals `issues`, `have_yq` and `elsewhere_names`, and nothing else**, which the header names, and a comment on `run_doctor`'s `local issues=0 elsewhere_names=" "` names again; `have_yq` keeps the comment it has. Every check adds to `issues` with the line it has today, `issues=$((issues + 1))`; the utilities and dependencies checks read `have_yq`; the utilities check fills `elsewhere_names` for the dependencies check to skip what runs elsewhere (issue 0083). Bash's dynamic scope carries them, in 3.2 as in 5, with no nameref and no new global. `elsewhere_names=" "` moves from the utilities section's `local` line to `run_doctor`'s.
- **No count through an exit status**: each check ends `return 0`, and none has a could-not-run case, since every fault it meets today is a line and an issue. A command that fails inside a check still ends doctor under `bin/utilz`'s errexit, as it does inline today; 0110 fixes the ones that do.
- **Every other variable keeps its scope**: each check declares local what its section declares today, and the dependencies check also declares `name`, which `run_doctor` declares once, in the utilities section, and the dependency walk reuses. The names today's code never declares (`dir`, `util`, `dep_info`) stay undeclared: declaring them changes nothing doctor prints, and it is not this change.
- **`install.sh` is sourced where it is today**, in the PATH check (the link set's health) and the integrity check. Its top level assigns globals (`INSTALL_GH`, `INSTALL_CI_WORKFLOW` and `INSTALL_CI_DEADLINE`, and `INSTALL_BREW`), and nothing in doctor's call chain declares those names local, so they land global when a check sources it, as they do from `run_doctor` today (vc's read, 26 Oct).
- **PFIC: nothing new is split, because nowhere pays.** The I/O-free decisions are functions of their own already, outside `run_doctor`, and each check keeps calling them. Which tree this is is `utilz_tree`'s answer, which the version line, install's target check, prez's shim and menuz also ask; the check maps it to a line, and reads git only in the dev arm. Whether a manifest is current is `install_manifest_check`'s status; the check maps it to a line, and asks `utilz_tree` only for the old-form status or a tree with no manifest. Which dependencies are missing is `dependency_present`'s answer, entry by entry, in a walk that stops early: an entry's `install` and `required` are read only once it is missing. Reading at the check's edge would run reads that do not run today, and 0110 shows that such a read can end doctor, so the report would change on a fixture where today it does not.
- **Comments**: each section's comments go with it, and its `# Check:` line becomes the function's header. Install integrity's section, which a rule line set off inline, takes `# Check: Install integrity` as its header instead. `each_utility`'s list of its consumers (common.sh, "run_doctor twice") names the installed utilities and external dependencies checks instead, and `emacs_doctor`'s note that its verdict matches `run_doctor` names the external dependencies check. The header says each check prints its closing blank line, but for the external dependencies check, whose blank line is the install integrity check's leading one, as it was inline; and the installed utilities check's comment on `elsewhere_lines` says the padded names now live in `run_doctor`'s `elsewhere_names`.
- **Carried comments that break the house rules are corrected in the same pass**: the PATH check's header counted the ways to have a working install and named one by its position, and it names them now, this tree's `bin/` on PATH or a `utilz` on PATH that is this tree's; the external dependencies check's note on where its verdict prints named checks by their step numbers, and it names them now; and the install integrity check's note that install.sh is kept off the utilities' hot path, and the runtime set's exclusion note near the top of common.sh, outside doctor, each wrote how many utilities there are, and those counts are deleted.
- **The move is mechanical**: a script moves each section verbatim, from its marker comment to the blank line before the next, and refuses if a marker or a line it changes is not where it expects; the comment corrections above are made by hand on its output, and touch comments only. Sorted, the lines of common.sh before and after differ only in the functions' own lines (the header, each `_doctor_check_<name>() {`, `return 0` and `}`, and each call in `run_doctor`), the comments named above, and the `local` lines of `run_doctor` and the installed utilities check, between which `elsewhere_names` moves, and of the external dependencies check, which declares `name`. No check reads a variable another check declares local, other than the locals `run_doctor` shares.
- **CHANGELOG**: one line under 2.14.4's harness and development notes, saying that doctor's report and its exit status do not change.
- **The proof, in one heavy for 0111 and 0110 together**, booked through utilz-vc with molt-vc after vc's critic leg: the whole utilz suite green on 0111, unchanged, and on 0111 plus 0110, with 0110's tests, and install_e2e, which refuses a linked worktree, in a full clone; `bin/utilz doctor` on the dev tree at 0109's close (`0946cd4f`) and at 0111's commit, diffed, differing only in the version line's sha, with the same exit status; and the same before-and-after diff of the whole report and exit status on doctor fixtures built as tree.bats builds them (a current opt install, an old keg, a manifestless keg under brew's opt link, a dev tree git cannot read, a tree Utilz cannot name), which the suite drives but asserts only in part, at `0946cd4f`, at 0111 and at 0111 plus 0110, where no read fails, so 0110 changes nothing either.
- **0110 on top**, in `_doctor_check_dependencies`, as its body says: red on the 0111 commit, green with the fix.

## Scope

2.14.4, by hv's word. cc's: one worktree, wt-0109 detached on 0109's close (`0946cd4f`) so that prez's build stands, with 0111 then 0110 as two commits, banked for utilz-vc's read and critic leg before the heavy. Each lands by path, is checked by its change, and closes. The twins and the dry run then run on the final head. Size: M (cc's estimate).
